items.passage: Kites do not haggle. My landlord, Faris, does, and for eleven years I have rented the room above his yard in Beirut and watched him do it with every buyer who climbs the stairs. Bamboo, paper, glue: he prices each one as if it were gold leaf, then throws in a tail for free and calls it charity. So when a developer offered to buy the yard, the house, and my room, I assumed I would be treated to the performance of a lifetime. Instead Faris, who shares the deed with his brother abroad, sat on an overturned crate and said nothing for a long while. Then he showed me the diamond kite his father had built the year they arrived, its frame mended so often that hardly any of the first wood remains. I had thought of the yard as a stage for his bargaining. That evening it looked more like a ledger of everything his family had refused to let go.
items.question: Which choice best describes the shift in tone that occurs in the text?
options: It shifts from wry amusement to tenderness.
It shifts from open anger to calm indifference.
It shifts from solemn grief to cheerful resolve.
It shifts from firm certainty to bewildered panic.
items.explanation: 앞부분에서 화자는 대나무와 종이를 금박처럼 값 매기다 꼬리를 공짜로 얹어 주는 Faris의 흥정을 재치 있게 묘사하며 일생일대의 공연을 기대한다. 그러나 매각 제안을 받은 Faris가 말없이 앉아 수없이 고친 아버지의 연을 보여 주자, 화자는 마당을 가족이 지켜 온 것의 장부로 보게 되므로 A가 정답이다. D는 화자의 예상이 빗나간 점에 주목하지만 당황이나 공포는 드러나지 않는다. B와 C는 지문에 없는 분노나 명랑한 결심을 가정한다.

items.passage: Why did his grandmother always cook two portions of fish curry when the ferry crew numbered only eleven? Arjun had wondered this since his first season in the galley of the river ferry out of Dhaka. Each evening she ladled twelve bowls, covered the last with a tin plate, and set it on the shelf by the porthole. By morning it was empty and scrubbed. Arjun assumed a rat, or a greedy deckhand, and said nothing. Then one night he stayed awake behind the rice sacks and saw his uncle Ishaan, whom the family spoke of as lost in debt and shame, climb through the cargo hatch and eat in silence. His grandmother sat beside him, mending a net, and did not look up. In the morning Arjun asked her nothing. He only covered the twelfth bowl himself, and set it by the porthole.
items.question: Which choice best describes the overall structure of the text?
options: A conflict between two crew members is introduced and then settled by the grandmother.
A family memory is recounted and then contrasted with a failure in the present day.
A plan the grandson devises is described step by step and then shown to fail.
A puzzling routine is presented, and a discovery then explains and continues it.
items.explanation: 지문은 왜 할머니가 늘 한 그릇을 더 담는지 묻는 질문으로 시작해, 열두 번째 그릇을 덮어 두는 반복된 일상을 묘사한다. 이어 Arjun이 밤에 몰래 지켜보다 숨어 지내는 삼촌 Ishaan을 발견하면서 일상의 이유가 밝혀지고, 마지막에는 Arjun이 직접 그릇을 덮어 그 침묵을 이어 가므로 D가 정답이다. C는 Arjun이 숨어서 지켜본 행동을 계획으로 보지만 그 계획은 실패하지 않고 오히려 진실을 드러낸다. A와 B는 선원 간 갈등이나 현재의 실패처럼 지문에 없는 요소를 가정한다.

items.passage: Siti had worked at the seed-saving cooperative in Hanoi for two years before her aunt spoke to her about anything except labels. Nguyen ran the drying room like a clinic. Seeds were weighed, sealed, and dated; packets were stacked by month; mistakes were corrected with a finger tapping the shelf, never a word. Siti learned the work by watching that finger. She cooked lunch for the volunteers and ate hers alone on the steps. Then, one wet afternoon, she found an unlabeled jar of small black beans behind the rice drawers and began, as she had been taught, to write unknown. Nguyen took the pen from her. These were your mother's, she said. She grew them on the roof the year you were born, and I have not been able to say her name in this room since. She wrote it on the label herself, slowly, and handed the pen back.
items.question: Which choice best describes the overall structure of the text?
options: It describes a long, wordless routine and then presents the moment it is broken.
It recounts a sharp argument and then explains the misunderstanding behind it.
It contrasts two workplaces and then explains why one character prefers the first.
It introduces a mystery about a jar and then leaves the jar's origin unresolved.
items.explanation: 지문 앞부분은 라벨 외에는 말이 없는 숙모, 손가락으로만 실수를 고치는 방식, 혼자 점심을 먹는 Siti 등 오랜 침묵 속 일상을 자세히 묘사한다. 이후 라벨 없는 콩 항아리를 계기로 Nguyen이 Siti의 어머니 이야기를 꺼내며 침묵이 깨지므로 A가 정답이다. D는 항아리가 등장한다는 점에서 그럴듯하지만 콩의 출처는 어머니의 것으로 밝혀진다. B와 C는 지문에 없는 말다툼이나 두 일터의 대비를 가정한다.

items.passage: Salt keeps nothing secret. On the flats outside Marrakesh it shows every footprint, every drag of a rake, and so the whole crew saw Malek stop when Lindiwe arrived with the old rake-master's wooden rake on her shoulder. She was nineteen, three weeks on the job, and the old man's granddaughter; the rake had come to her in his will. Malek assigned her the farthest pan and said nothing about it. __When he took off his gloves at noon, the ridges across his palms matched, groove for groove, the worn places on that handle, where for twenty years he had pulled it beside the old man.__ Lindiwe noticed. She worked the far pan until dusk, then walked back across the white crust and leaned the rake against Malek's shed. It pulls left, she told him. You will know how to correct it. He did not thank her, but the next morning he moved her pan closer to his own.
items.question: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
options: It suggests that Malek is too exhausted to work alongside the rest of the crew.
It shows that Lindiwe has already mastered the rake despite her short time there.
It indicates that the rake was badly damaged before Lindiwe inherited it.
It reveals the personal history behind Malek's reaction to the inheritance.
items.explanation: 밑줄 문장 앞에서 Malek은 Lindiwe가 물려받은 갈퀴를 보고 멈춰 서고 그녀를 가장 먼 염전에 배치하지만, 그 이유는 설명되지 않는다. 밑줄 문장은 그의 손바닥 굳은살이 20년 동안 스승 곁에서 그 갈퀴를 잡아 생긴 자국과 들어맞는다고 보여 주어 그의 반응 뒤에 있는 개인사를 드러내므로 D가 정답이다. 이 정보를 알아챈 Lindiwe가 갈퀴를 돌려주는 이후 행동도 이 해석을 뒷받침한다. C는 손잡이의 닳은 자국을 손상으로 오해했고, A와 B는 피로나 Lindiwe의 숙련도처럼 밑줄 문장이 다루지 않는 내용이다.

items.passage: What do you tell a seven-year-old when the money stops? Hassan asked it of no one as he pushed his delivery bicycle across the dried riverbed on the edge of Lagos, the crates of bread rattling behind him. Since his father's shop had closed, he had been telling his little sister that their father was traveling for business. Seoyeon, the widow who bought six loaves every Friday, was waiting at the far bank. She had overheard his sister boasting about the trip. __Children forgive the hard truth sooner than they forgive the kind lie, she said, because the lie tells them they were not trusted.__ Hassan wanted to argue, but she had already turned toward her gate. That evening he sat his sister on the step, gave her the heel of the last loaf, and told her, carefully, that their father was home every day now and was looking for work, and that the family would need her help.
items.question: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
options: It offers advice that Hassan resists at first but later follows.
It explains why Seoyeon has decided to stop buying bread from Hassan.
It reveals that Seoyeon once misled her own children about money.
It shows that Hassan's sister already knows the truth about the shop.
items.explanation: 앞부분에서 Hassan은 어린 여동생에게 아버지가 출장 중이라고 거짓말해 왔고, 무엇을 말해야 할지 고민한다. 밑줄 문장에서 Seoyeon은 친절한 거짓말보다 힘든 진실이 낫다고 조언하고, Hassan은 반박하고 싶어 하지만 그날 저녁 여동생에게 사실을 털어놓으므로 A가 정답이다. C는 Seoyeon이 과부라는 점에서 그럴듯한 추측이지만 그녀 자신의 과거에 대한 근거는 없다. B와 D는 빵 구매 중단이나 여동생이 이미 진실을 안다는 등 지문과 맞지 않는 내용이다.

items.passage: "You are the one with the map, then," the farmer said as I took the seat beside her on the night bus out of Sapporo. Her name was Chiyo, and she had recognized the city survey office's logo on my tube of drawings. I am Aiko; I mark where roads will go. For an hour she told me, without bitterness, about the cherry tree at the corner of her field, and about the promise she had made to her granddaughter that it would bloom there until the girl was grown. I knew the corner. My line ran through it. __Somewhere past Asahikawa, I unrolled the drawing on my knees and folded it so that the small red cross over her field disappeared into the crease.__ I told myself it was only to keep the paper from sliding. In the morning I filed my report as written. But I asked my supervisor, for the first time in six years, whether the line could bend.
items.question: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
options: It shows the narrator deciding to destroy the survey drawing in secret.
It signals the narrator's first private unease about her assignment.
It indicates that the narrator was careless with her official documents.
It reveals that Chiyo had asked the narrator directly to alter the map.
items.explanation: 밑줄 문장 앞에서 화자는 자신의 측량선이 Chiyo가 손녀에게 지키겠다고 약속한 벚나무를 지난다는 사실을 안다. 밑줄 문장에서 화자는 들판 위 빨간 표시가 접힌 선 속으로 사라지게 도면을 접는데, 이는 자기 임무에 대한 첫 번째 남모를 불편함을 보여 주므로 B가 정답이다. 이후 6년 만에 처음으로 선을 휠 수 있는지 묻는 행동이 이를 뒷받침한다. A는 도면을 접는 행동을 파기로 과장했고, C와 D는 부주의나 Chiyo의 직접 요청처럼 지문에 없는 내용이다.

items.passage: We split the house our mother left us the way she had taught us to split a bolt of cloth at the weaving cooperative: measure twice, cut once, argue never. Marcus took the kitchen and the back porch. I took the front rooms and the loom. When the cooperative's director called to say that Marcus's quilt had been chosen for the state museum, he shrugged into the phone and said it was just scraps. He told me the same thing that night, twice, while we taped boxes. He said the museum probably needed something to fill a wall. __Yet when he packed the quilt to send it, he folded it so that the little muslin tag stitched with his name lay on top, square in the center, where anyone opening the box would see it first.__ I did not mention it. I only wrote fragile on the box in my best letters, and let him think I had not noticed.
items.question: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
options: It suggests that Marcus plans to keep the quilt rather than send it.
It explains why the brothers chose to divide the house the way they did.
It provides a detail that quietly undercuts Marcus's claim of indifference.
It reveals that the narrator resents the attention his brother is receiving.
items.explanation: 밑줄 문장 앞에서 Marcus는 박물관 선정 소식에 어깨를 으쓱하며 퀼트가 그저 자투리라고 여러 번 말한다. 그러나 밑줄 문장에서 그는 자기 이름이 수놓인 태그가 상자를 연 사람에게 가장 먼저 보이도록 퀼트를 접으므로, 무관심하다는 그의 주장을 은근히 뒤집는 세부 묘사라는 C가 정답이다. 화자가 이를 알아채고도 모르는 척하는 마지막 장면도 이 해석을 뒷받침한다. D는 형제 사이 관계에 주목하지만 화자는 원망이 아니라 너그러움을 보이며, A와 B는 지문과 맞지 않는다.

items.passage: Pins bristled from Freja's sleeve like the quills of a small, offended animal as she marched the length of the summer camp dining hall in Rotterdam, inspecting the costumes laid out on the long tables. She had sewn for the camp's play for thirty summers and had never once let an apprentice cut the cloth. Thorvald, her only apprentice, sixteen and earnest, had asked every morning for a week. Every morning she had told him his hands were too hasty, and every afternoon she had left the good shears, quite by accident, a little closer to his end of the table. On the eighth day she announced, to the rafters rather than to him, that her wrists ached and that someone might as well ruin the velvet as let it sit. Then she sat down with her tea and pretended, with tremendous concentration, not to watch his first cut.
items.question: Which choice best describes the narrator's attitude toward Freja?
options: Open scorn for her refusal to share her craft
Affectionate amusement at her stubborn pride
Detached neutrality toward her daily routine
Anxious pity for her failing health and wrists
items.explanation: 서술자는 Freja의 소매에 꽂힌 핀을 기분 상한 작은 동물의 가시에 비유하고, 그녀가 '우연히' 가위를 Thorvald 쪽으로 옮겨 두는 모습을 짓궂게 묘사한다. 또 손목이 아프다며 서까래에 대고 선언하거나 엄청난 집중력으로 보지 않는 척하는 장면에서 고집스러운 자존심을 다정하게 웃으며 바라보는 태도가 드러나므로 B가 정답이다. D는 손목 통증 언급에 주목하지만 이는 체면을 지키려는 핑계로 그려진다. A와 C는 서술의 따뜻한 유머를 놓친 선택지다.

items.passage: Forty-one letters, two rubber bands, one shoebox: that was what Ama carried into the empty classroom at the language school in Accra where she now taught French in the evenings. Our mother had written them to me, Seun, during my six years at university abroad, and Ama had kept them after the funeral. We read them at a student's desk under the buzzing tube light. In every letter our mother praised my examinations. In almost every letter, near the end, she mentioned in passing that Ama had taken another shift at the market, or had postponed her own course for another year. I had read those lines at the time and skimmed past them. Now Ama read them aloud in an even voice, smoothing each page flat, and when she reached the one about the year she gave up her scholarship, she only said that the handwriting was very neat that month. I could not look at her, and I could not look away.
items.question: Which choice best describes the narrator's attitude toward Ama?
options: Resentful envy of the praise Ama now receives
Amused tolerance of Ama's careful habits
Remorseful admiration for Ama's sacrifice
Cautious suspicion of Ama's reasons for sharing
items.explanation: 화자는 어머니의 편지 끝에 적힌 Ama의 희생에 관한 문장을 예전에는 건너뛰었다고 고백해 뒤늦은 자책을 드러낸다. 동시에 장학금을 포기한 해의 편지를 읽으면서도 글씨가 단정하다고만 말하는 Ama의 담담함을 바라보며, 그녀를 볼 수도 외면할 수도 없다고 말하므로 C가 정답이다. D는 Ama가 상자를 가져온 의도를 의심할 수 있다는 점에서 그럴듯하지만 지문에 의심의 근거는 없다. A와 B는 질투나 가벼운 관용처럼 화자의 무거운 감정과 맞지 않는다.

items.passage:
Folding chairs in rows on the gymnasium floor,
the Lima heat pressing through the high windows,
and I in my borrowed white, braced
for Renata, Santiago's mother,
who had said, the week before, that I was too young
to know what I was promising.
I had rehearsed my answers to her like a debate.
But when the sound system shrieked and died
and the aunts began to murmur,
it was Renata who climbed onto a bench,
her good shoes in one hand,
and sang the first hymn without a microphone
until the whole room followed.
Later she pinned my slipping veil
with a clip from her own hair
and told me, gruffly, that she had been too young once, too.
I keep that clip in a dish by the door.
I still do not know all her reasons.
I know whose voice filled the room
when mine would not come.
items.question: Which choice best describes the speaker's attitude toward Renata?
options: Lingering suspicion of Renata's true motives
Playful mockery of Renata's gruff manner
Polite indifference toward Renata's gestures
Newfound gratitude that replaces wariness
items.explanation: 시의 앞부분에서 화자는 자신이 너무 어리다고 말했던 시어머니 Renata에게 대비하며 토론처럼 답변을 연습했다고 말해 경계심을 드러낸다. 그러나 음향 장비가 고장 나자 Renata가 의자에 올라 찬송을 이끌고 자기 머리핀으로 면사포를 고정해 주며, 화자는 그 핀을 지금도 간직하고 목소리가 나오지 않을 때 누구의 목소리가 방을 채웠는지 안다고 말하므로 D가 정답이다. A는 '모든 이유를 알지는 못한다'는 구절을 근거로 하지만, 이는 의심보다 감사의 맥락에서 나온다. B와 C는 화자의 깊은 고마움을 놓친다.

items.passage: Bleach, damp plaster, and the neighbor's frying onions filled the stairwell of our building in Galicia the evening my brother came home. Sergio climbed the four flights slowly, as if counting them, and stopped on each landing to touch the rail. I, Chiara, had planned the anniversary for weeks: a dinner for our father's old friends, candles, his favorite songs on the record player. Sergio listened to the plan on the third-floor landing and said he could not sit in a room full of people tonight. I wanted to argue. Instead I noticed how he kept his back to the wall, and how his hand flinched when a door banged above us. So I cancelled the dinner by text, one guest at a time, while he waited beside me. We marked the day on the stairs instead, sharing a single candle and our father's harmonica, which neither of us could play, until the timer light clicked off and we did not bother to turn it on again.
items.question: Which choice best describes the narrator's attitude toward Sergio?
options: Protective tenderness toward his fragile state
Resentful impatience with his refusal of her plan
Bemused detachment from his unusual behavior
Fearful awe of his experiences as a soldier
items.explanation: 화자는 Sergio가 계단을 세듯 천천히 오르고 벽에 등을 붙이며 문 소리에 움찔하는 모습을 세심하게 관찰한다. 몇 주 준비한 저녁 모임을 반대하고 싶었지만 그의 상태를 보고 손님에게 하나씩 취소 문자를 보내며 계단에서 함께 기일을 보내므로, 연약한 오빠를 보호하려는 다정함이라는 A가 정답이다. B는 화자가 처음에 따지고 싶었다는 부분을 근거로 하지만 그녀는 곧 그 마음을 접는다. C와 D는 화자의 관찰이 지닌 따뜻한 관심을 무관심이나 두려움으로 잘못 읽었다.

items.passage: Why did I never ask Amelie for the scissors back? Her uncle's tailoring shop on Chicago's South Side had a back room that smelled of steam and chalk, and that was where she first lent me the brass-handled shears, the summer my family moved onto her block. I was Colby, the new boy who cut paper stars badly, and she said a good tool would fix my hands. It did not, but I kept the shears through two more moves and a decade of silence between us. Each time I unpacked them, I meant to write to her. Instead I would oil the hinge, test the blades on a scrap of newsprint, and set them back in their drawer as if they were still on loan. Last spring a cousin mentioned that Amelie now runs the shop herself. I bought a card that week; it is still blank, propped against the window above my desk.
items.question: Which choice best describes the narrator's attitude toward his friendship with Amelie?
options: Resentful, since he takes her silence about the shears as proof she forgot him
Affectionate toward the friendship yet sheepish about his long delay in reaching out
Proud, chiefly of having kept the shears in good condition through several moves
Indifferent, treating the shears as an ordinary tool rather than a reminder of her
items.explanation: 화자는 가위를 '아직 빌린 것처럼' 기름칠해 보관하며 매번 편지를 쓰려 했다고 말해 우정에 대한 애정을 드러낸다. 동시에 10년의 침묵, 사 놓고 아직 비어 있는 카드는 연락을 미뤄 온 데 대한 머쓱함과 망설임을 보여 준다. 따라서 두 단서를 함께 읽은 B가 정답이다. A의 원망, C의 물건 보관에 대한 자부심, D의 무관심은 지문의 단서와 맞지 않는다.

items.passage:
By the time you receive this, dear Samira, the barber on Calle Obispo will have swept up the last of my hair and, I hope, the last of our argument. You insisted the mirror in his Havana shop hung crooked; I insisted it was the floor. We spent an entire afternoon on it, you tapping your cane like a gavel, I quoting the level I had borrowed from the clerk's office. I see now that neither of us cared about the mirror. You were hurt that I had accepted the post in Santiago without consulting you, and I was annoyed that I still wanted your blessing. Forgive the clumsy way I argued. You taught me that a ruling should be stated plainly, and here is mine: I am going, and I will write every month. The barber says the mirror has hung that way since 1921, and he refuses to straighten it.
Moira
items.question: Which choice best describes Moira's attitude toward Samira in the letter?
options: Defiant, dismissing Samira's past guidance as irrelevant to her new career

### lit40-medium-04-026 — skill text_structure_purpose · 유형 tone_shift
[지문]
Kites do not haggle. My landlord, Faris, does, and for eleven years I have rented the room above his yard in Beirut and watched him do it with every buyer who climbs the stairs. Bamboo, paper, glue: he prices each one as if it were gold leaf, then throws in a tail for free and calls it charity. So when a developer offered to buy the yard, the house, and my room, I assumed I would be treated to the performance of a lifetime. Instead Faris, who shares the deed with his brother abroad, sat on an overturned crate and said nothing for a long while. Then he showed me the diamond kite his father had built the year they arrived, its frame mended so often that hardly any of the first wood remains. I had thought of the yard as a stage for his bargaining. That evening it looked more like a ledger of everything his family had refused to let go.

[질문] Which choice best describes the shift in tone that occurs in the text?
A) It shifts from wry amusement to tenderness.
B) It shifts from open anger to calm indifference.
C) It shifts from solemn grief to cheerful resolve.
D) It shifts from firm certainty to bewildered panic.

[표시된 정답] A
[해설]
앞부분에서 화자는 대나무와 종이를 금박처럼 값 매기다 꼬리를 공짜로 얹어 주는 Faris의 흥정을 재치 있게 묘사하며 일생일대의 공연을 기대한다. 그러나 매각 제안을 받은 Faris가 말없이 앉아 수없이 고친 아버지의 연을 보여 주자, 화자는 마당을 가족이 지켜 온 것의 장부로 보게 되므로 A가 정답이다. D는 화자의 예상이 빗나간 점에 주목하지만 당황이나 공포는 드러나지 않는다. B와 C는 지문에 없는 분노나 명랑한 결심을 가정한다.
### lit40-medium-04-029 — skill text_structure_purpose · 유형 text_structure
[지문]
Why did his grandmother always cook two portions of fish curry when the ferry crew numbered only eleven? Arjun had wondered this since his first season in the galley of the river ferry out of Dhaka. Each evening she ladled twelve bowls, covered the last with a tin plate, and set it on the shelf by the porthole. By morning it was empty and scrubbed. Arjun assumed a rat, or a greedy deckhand, and said nothing. Then one night he stayed awake behind the rice sacks and saw his uncle Ishaan, whom the family spoke of as lost in debt and shame, climb through the cargo hatch and eat in silence. His grandmother sat beside him, mending a net, and did not look up. In the morning Arjun asked her nothing. He only covered the twelfth bowl himself, and set it by the porthole.

[질문] Which choice best describes the overall structure of the text?
A) A conflict between two crew members is introduced and then settled by the grandmother.
B) A family memory is recounted and then contrasted with a failure in the present day.
C) A plan the grandson devises is described step by step and then shown to fail.
D) A puzzling routine is presented, and a discovery then explains and continues it.

[표시된 정답] D
[해설]
지문은 왜 할머니가 늘 한 그릇을 더 담는지 묻는 질문으로 시작해, 열두 번째 그릇을 덮어 두는 반복된 일상을 묘사한다. 이어 Arjun이 밤에 몰래 지켜보다 숨어 지내는 삼촌 Ishaan을 발견하면서 일상의 이유가 밝혀지고, 마지막에는 Arjun이 직접 그릇을 덮어 그 침묵을 이어 가므로 D가 정답이다. C는 Arjun이 숨어서 지켜본 행동을 계획으로 보지만 그 계획은 실패하지 않고 오히려 진실을 드러낸다. A와 B는 선원 간 갈등이나 현재의 실패처럼 지문에 없는 요소를 가정한다.
### lit40-medium-04-030 — skill text_structure_purpose · 유형 text_structure
[지문]
Siti had worked at the seed-saving cooperative in Hanoi for two years before her aunt spoke to her about anything except labels. Nguyen ran the drying room like a clinic. Seeds were weighed, sealed, and dated; packets were stacked by month; mistakes were corrected with a finger tapping the shelf, never a word. Siti learned the work by watching that finger. She cooked lunch for the volunteers and ate hers alone on the steps. Then, one wet afternoon, she found an unlabeled jar of small black beans behind the rice drawers and began, as she had been taught, to write unknown. Nguyen took the pen from her. These were your mother's, she said. She grew them on the roof the year you were born, and I have not been able to say her name in this room since. She wrote it on the label herself, slowly, and handed the pen back.

[질문] Which choice best describes the overall structure of the text?
A) It describes a long, wordless routine and then presents the moment it is broken.
B) It recounts a sharp argument and then explains the misunderstanding behind it.
C) It contrasts two workplaces and then explains why one character prefers the first.
D) It introduces a mystery about a jar and then leaves the jar's origin unresolved.

[표시된 정답] A
[해설]
지문 앞부분은 라벨 외에는 말이 없는 숙모, 손가락으로만 실수를 고치는 방식, 혼자 점심을 먹는 Siti 등 오랜 침묵 속 일상을 자세히 묘사한다. 이후 라벨 없는 콩 항아리를 계기로 Nguyen이 Siti의 어머니 이야기를 꺼내며 침묵이 깨지므로 A가 정답이다. D는 항아리가 등장한다는 점에서 그럴듯하지만 콩의 출처는 어머니의 것으로 밝혀진다. B와 C는 지문에 없는 말다툼이나 두 일터의 대비를 가정한다.
### lit40-medium-04-033 — skill text_structure_purpose · 유형 underlined_portion_function

Salt keeps nothing secret. On the flats outside Marrakesh it shows every footprint, every drag of a rake, and so the whole crew saw Malek stop when Lindiwe arrived with the old rake-master's wooden rake on her shoulder. She was nineteen, three weeks on the job, and the old man's granddaughter; the rake had come to her in his will. Malek assigned her the farthest pan and said nothing about it. __When he took off his gloves at noon, the ridges across his palms matched, groove for groove, the worn places on that handle, where for twenty years he had pulled it beside the old man.__ Lindiwe noticed. She worked the far pan until dusk, then walked back across the white crust and leaned the rake against Malek's shed. It pulls left, she told him. You will know how to correct it. He did not thank her, but the next morning he moved her pan closer to his own.
